J'ai regardé un let's play de ce jeu il y a 9 ans, autant dire que j'en avais oublié beaucoup de détails, notamment sa fin. 
Etant donné qu'il est sorti il y a plus de 10ans je ne sais pas si beaucoup de personnes l'ont acheté pendant les dernières années, mais au cas où vous découvriez totalement ce jeu, je recommanderais de se fier surtout aux images de ce jeu plutôt qu'aux parties animées du trailer, qui ont été ajoutées pour en faire la promotion. 

Personnellement, le style graphique m'a beaucoup attiré à l'époque et c'est toujours le cas aujourd'hui. Le design des personnages et leurs caractéristiques sont assez attrayants si on apprécie les esthétiques de l'étrange (particulièrement les designs de bébés que je trouve troublants). 
Du côté de l'histoire, en l'ayant oublié, j'ai eu un changement de théorie pendant le jeu qui révèle de manière plutôt fluide selon moi des informations sur notre personnage principal et sur les créatures qui l'entourent à travers des dialogues et d'éléments visuels. Certains personnages restent assez peu détaillés, mais il faut garder en tête que le jeu est plutôt court et centré sur l'histoire de notre personnage. 
La majorité des énigmes sont simples et plutôt intuitives, même si j'ai aussi rencontré des difficultés dans la dernière partie du jeu comme d'autres joueurs, qui peut être un peu longue et répétitive tout en étant floue.

“In order to design good horror, first make sure that you, yourself, are not a coward”. These are the words that echoed in my mind when I sat down and asked myself what I think of Stray Cat Crossing.

And honestly, kudos to my brain [strike]despite the dramatics[/strike], because that pretty much sums up how I see this game rather perfectly. On multiple occasions, the game sets up something (a scene, a trope, a theme, build-up), and absolutely flirts HARD with the dark, the twisted, the macabre, the tragic, and as soon as it is actually seduced, and JUST as its about to slyly walk in, panting, smiling and unblinking, the game blushes, yelps, and slams the door on its face like a bashful maiden who bit more than she can chew. 

This game is like a sadist in a BDSM relationship, who doesn’t have the heart to actually prolong the torture, despite the sub willing and practically begging for it. The kind that thinks they went too far, 15 minutes into foreplay. There is this sickening compulsion, I feel, to quickly resolve any tension build-up, almost like the devs themselves got too scared with what they wrote mid-developing. Worse yet, without delving into spoilers, there are even sections that get a wholesome resolution, and no, not as a surprisingly bittersweet moment in what is otherwise a gloomy atmosphere, dark-souls style. No, it seems that this is the game’s modus operendi; the moments that don’t get a wholesome resolution, is because the dev couldn’t fit it into the timeslot.

Don’t get me wrong, review-reader-who’s-about-to-call-me-an-edgelord: I completely and utterly understand that not all horror games need to be twisted and dark; I practically made a career of absolutely tearing a new one into devs who go too edgy with their horror games for its own sake. If anything, I’m saying this game is trying to go too Tumblr-creepy with its aesthetics and motifs, for its own sake. And that’s the keyword here: “for its own sake”. When you don’t let things cook, when you resolve them too quickly, when you don’t see a tragedy all the way to its wrenching end, then you started it over nothing. You started it “for the vibes”. 

And speaking of vibes, I know that you’re interested in this game for its art style, just like I was. First of all, the art doesn’t particularly get better? What you see in the screenshots is, more or less, what you’ll get. And secondly, while I will not accuse someone of plagiarism without proof (because it genuinely goes against my ethics), so I won’t say it’s intentional, BUT AM I THE ONLY ONE NOTICING THAT THE TRAILER SONG IS LITERALLY KINGDOM HEARTS’ “MY SANCTUARY”? If it is not intentional (and I will not assume so without proof), then at the very least, it disappointingly shows where the devs picked up their vibes-centric design philosophy inspiration.

On a side note, this review was genuinely painful to write. I hate tearing THIS hard into a small studio. I don’t feel bad if it’s a bigger studio, even if indie. It’s a bunch of kids (regardless of age, and not derogatory) who want to have fun and design a game. But as much as it pains me to tear into them like that, I have to be honest. If my review did not dissuade you from buying the game, and you still find yourself curious, then by all means, don’t let me stop you. If you have love for them, don’t hold it back.

[b][u]Stray Cat Crossing[/u][/b] – это странноватое, крафтовое, сюрреалистические, психологическое приключение с элементами хоррора, в 2D исполнении, созданное в RPG Maker, в азиатском сеттинге, которое способно обратить на себя внимание, отринув все возможные сожалению о потраченном зря времени.






[h1][b]==========[/b][/h1]
[quote][b]Введение:[/b][/quote]
Без вступления. Под шум ночным насекомых. Мы оказываемся посреди поляны с деревьями в роли красноволосой девочки подростка. Нашими руками мы выводим девочку к проезжей части, где не ездит ни одна машина, пройдя которую, обнаруживаем на другой стороне маленькую рыжую девочку в раскидистой белой шляпе и бело-зелёном платье. Мелкая усиленно льёт слёзы, не замечая наше приближение, однако под нашим управление девочка подросток выясняет, что мелкую зовут Кэт, она испугана и хочет домой. Красноволосая предлагает помощь, чтобы довести её до дома, а также повязывает ей своё тёплый шарф, дабы мелкая не мёрзла. На сцену вступает странная гудящая музыкальная композиция, девочки двигаются по дороге к дому, попутно уворачиваясь от одной единственной машины за всё время. Чуть погодя, перед ними возвышается немаленьких размеров особнячок, где они прощаются друг с другом, Кэт убегает в дом, а красноволосая вспоминает, что она забыл забрать шарф обратно. Делать нечего, надо зайти в дом к Кэт и попросить вернуть шарф.
Вы – красноволосая девочка подросток. Ваша задача – вернуть шарф и двигаться дальше по своим делам.

Как уже упоминалось ранее, игра создана на движке RPG Maker при упоминании которого у многих в головах могут возникнуть однообразные, похожие друг на друга, но из разных игровых проектов образы. Pushing past the tones of twisted horror, this game paints a picture of grief, understanding, and acceptance. Despite a multitude of bizarre creatures, none are more frightening than the consistent sense of loss, guilt, and warring naivety through the eyes of young child.

The full game doesn’t take long to complete, but the puzzles can be challenging at times. The art, in particular, I found very unique. Reminiscent of Alice in Wonderland, you find yourself becoming not only familiar, but appreciative of the oddities within the world. As the horror melts away, the truth is left to find. It may be a long journey toward forgiveness, but it’s a road we all have to cross eventually.

In my search for hidden gem RPG Maker games, finding something truly meaningful and special like this game is a rarity. When I started playing, I was immediately charmed by the art style and the wonderfully twisted aesthetic. As I kept playing, the game kept surprising me with how creative it could be. And then, that magical moment occurs where it all begins to come together, and things start falling into place. It crafts one of the most meaningful and emotional experiences that could come from an RPG Maker game. It does get repetitive in the third act, but that might be the only complaint I have with this beautiful work of art of an experience. Games like this are what RPG Maker is to me: Beautiful pieces of art that can only exist because of an engine that makes it easy for those with a vision to get their ideas out there. If you love short stories, and especially if you love RPG Maker horror, play this game immediately. You'll fall in love.

I just finished this game after sitting on it for a while, and wanted to write a review since it's relatively indi and should get some more attention. Hm...I'm conflicted on this one. Aesthetic wise, this game is absolutely stunning with so many things for weirdcore horror fans to fall in love with. Whacky and zany characters whose appearances actively effect how they interact with the world for some good body horror or charming quirks, locations bursting with symbolic imagery that are twisted and shifted as the game goes on, the music is so good I wish they sold an OST, and a meaningful message placed beneath the surface of said weirdness. On paper, it sounds right up my alley, yet the execution is questionable, particularly in the writing department. 

[i]Stray Cat Crossing[/i] tries to tell a simple story, yet, ends up bungling it so much throughout with random imagery, unnecessary sequences, and confusing gameplay elements that, by the end, I couldn't really tell you what the point was at all, besides some theories. The game separates itself so harshly in terms of gameplay and story that any connection to the two is extremely shallow. The designs of character have so many tiny details that make no sense and muddle any symbolic imagery that was meant to be made with them. There's bits upon completion that made me think "yeah I can see that", always followed by a "wait, what?". Most of the connections were as simple as just "this weird thing is named after some important character, and put next to another important character" without any exploration of the more in depth reason for this in the character's mind. The script feels like a draft as there are several unimportant characters that are just there...story wise. Game wise, you need to do things for them in the form of puzzles, which wouldn't be a bad idea if any of them held any significance.

One second I am seeing something horrific, the next I am being told do so some menial chore that rarely made me face anything I was that discomforted by. The story and gameplay constantly bickered with the latter claiming these tasks were important to the characters, and the former showing they rarely made any sense. The game ends up feeling like a dream where, every time it gets really good and you're actually making progress, the dream suddenly shifts in a bizarre and random way that completely negates everything before it, giving me whiplash. And honestly, I could go to bat for that if it didn't impede on the story's buildup for me. Letting the main character be more reactive instead of sorely focused on her scarf despite everything she sees might have made the ups and downs feel more like an emotional journey than it currently does. I will admit [spoiler]I found the ending very emotional, able to feel the character's guilt with that final scene punching me right in the gut.[/spoiler] But the main character was so emotionless up until that point this section felt like its own short story rather than connecting to the overall game, which, in contrast, didn't really evoke as much feeling or intrigue from me as I had hoped it would. And even then this section was a confusing mess. 

The conclusion is effectively [spoiler]"your mother told you terrible stories and never hid the fact that she didn't want you. Your father was so emotionally distant you were forced to call him by his first name only" yet also, "but they went looking for you and loved you, don't be sad!"[/spoiler] And I want to believe this was intentional, that this contradiction [spoiler]and her not knowing the photographer's name shows she is still in denial about everything that happened to her. That those affirmations showed her going back into her cycle because she just couldn't take the memory, and showing the car crash with sinister music reveals this wasn't the good ending we thought it was.[/spoiler] Yet, nothing here gives me faith it wasn't just an accidental oversight on the part of the writers not knowing how to deliver a proper twist or write an unreliable narrator. To be clear, its fine if it's not that, they can tell whatever story they want. I just wish I was more clued in as a player with the very limited things I could do to actively "seek out" this lore. 

The fact of the matter is, this game [b]demands[/b] you interact with its story, and, yet, shudders at the idea of you ever touching it at all. There is no way to play this game without figuring out the "answers", you will not progress unless you take the questionable actions required of you to get the next bit of story. Which isn't bad on its own, I love games with multiple endings, but I will always have a big soft spot for linear experiences as well, so long as the creators are aware of this and use it to their benefit. A wild ride that forces you to do or see terrible things to torment the player can be outright terrifying, and help put the audience into the character's shoes, who often feel completely trapped. 

This title never acted "aware" to me, because, again, almost everything it made me interact with never added to the characters who were supposed to be at the forefront. Little hints were dropped here and there through the environment, only for the player to return to a quest giver completely devoid of this depth. And yet, I as the player am not doing these things because I am curious nor because it gives me an opportunity to see more, but because the characters, for whatever reason, will not budge until I do this small or random task. The gameplay consists of, "hey I know you're going through an emotional crisis I'm a part of, but, could you get me some popcorn?". And, again, that could work, it really could, creating a surrealist and unforgiving world that showcases how the main character feels about herself. But its not that the characters are purposefully not acknowledging it, they're just not acknowledging [i]anything[/i], except what leads me to the next area or puzzle. If a game has multiple endings and I want to know more about the story, its on me as a player to seek out that lore and be proactive inside the game's universe. But, when a game is this linear and, on top of that, treats its story as unimportant while pushing tedious to accomplish puzzles up until the end, there's no reason for me as a player to care. This is a horror game with a deep story, and that should have taken precedent. 

So, all in all, I just found this title to be pretty disappointing. The main story and artistic style are very good in concept, but they weren't made to tie into each other enough and, as is, feel like completely separate entities. The game is so short it can't do what it wants to do effectively. For those hoping for a deep, and entertaining weirdcore experience, I wouldn't really recommend this one. That being said, it's only $3, so if it does look even mildly interesting, you may enjoy the randomness more than I did.
